rule: Never use the browser's number input for money, percentages or counts. Use a text field that refuses disallowed characters while typing (no e/E/+/-, no spinner).
detail: Money: digits and exactly one dot, 2 decimals, symbol from the profile currency (never a literal $). Whole numbers and percentages: digits only, no dot. A fractional filter threshold may take one dot. Bounded values are capped while typing, not afterwards. When a field switches between money and percent, trim the carried value to what the new field accepts. Do not strip the dot from money (a bid is 0.35).
test: Type 1e5E.3-+x.9: money keeps 15.39, whole number keeps 15.

rule: Cell text either wraps or is truncated with an ellipsis plus a full-text tooltip; it is never clipped bare.
detail: Truncation is the default for body cells; a column that must wrap declares it. Style fragments that share a selector must be merged, not object-spread, or one silently erases the other.
test: Probe for text elements with hidden overflow, scrollWidth > clientWidth and no ellipsis: a listing must report none.

rule: Numeric columns: header aligned left like text columns; figures start under the header and right-align with each other; Total row figures align with the column's figures.
detail: Cells that hold an input (budget, bid editor) are exempt and keep their own width.
test: Per column: each figure block starts at the label's left edge, right edges equal, Total right edge equal.

rule: Render static parts immediately (toolbar, column headers, Total label, pager words); draw skeletons only for data in transit, in the shape and size of what replaces them. The table must not change height when rows arrive.
detail: Checkbox -> small rounded square, switch -> pill, text -> bar, avatar/flag -> disc, multi-line cell -> one skeleton masked into bars at the loaded positions. Skeleton row height equals the real row height (tallest content + cell padding); do not pin real row heights. Skeleton count equals page size (or the known count, e.g. 4/4/4/3 dashboard tables). The Total row is present while waiting (label + bars).
test: Hold the request, measure body rows and footer height, then repeat after data loads: skeleton row = real row, footer present.

rule: A table with a single skeleton row shows 'No records to display' in a row of the same height so the pager does not jump; the message is centred within the visible table width and sticks to the left when scrolled sideways.
detail: Never read container width during render for this message (hidden tabs report 0 and break the text one word per line); observe it with a resize observer.
test: Empty answer on a one-row table: pager position unchanged.

rule: Do not cover a lazy tab with a generic bar skeleton while its code loads, and do not statically import the table either. Preload every tab's code when the browser is idle so switching finds it ready.
detail: Direct link to a tab may still wait for one chunk (known gap).

rule: The address is a chain page -> tab -> sub-tab -> modal. A level is valid only under its parent; changing a level clears everything below it; invalid params are dropped with a replace (no history entry).
detail: In the URL: tab; sub-tab that picks a view; modal/panel that creates or edits an entity. NOT in the URL: tabs/modes inside a form, confirm dialogs, inline edit cards, filters, column pickers, popovers, view-only drawers, and modals whose payload is the current row selection. A sub-tab decided by data is not written, and an address naming a forbidden one is dropped only after the data has loaded. Build URLs only through one set of typed builders; keep one table of valid tabs/subs/modals.

rule: Opening a modal pushes a history entry (Back closes it, date range and page kept); closing replaces (Forward must not reopen it). A modal the user could not open (no permission, disabled button, wrong kind) is not opened by a link either. An id that resolves to nothing: toast once, drop the param, never show an empty form.
detail: Budget-rule modal id is Amazon's rule id, not a row id; the wrong one creates a second rule. Leaving a page strips both pages' tab/sub/modal params.

rule: Each tab of a shared page keeps its own search/filters/sort/page under a prefix (the first tab keeps bare names); account, date range and page size are shared. Query strings are written readably (/, :, comma stay literal).
detail: Without a prefix a new tab would read the first tab's search.

rule: A new listing has the column set and order of the screen it replaces and nothing extra; the user's saved order wins, 'Reset order' returns to the default.
detail: Column menu: show/hide with Hide all/Show all, drag reorder, two fixed pin positions per row (left and right; the active side lit; click again to unpin), Unpin all. Move/pin/resize are disabled only on touch pointers, never by window width. Gaps against the old product are named in hand-off, not filled with something else.

rule: A tick shows in the same frame as the click; selection survives paging; a maximum is enforced at tick time (campaigns 300, child tabs 100, export-selected 1000, products-to-campaign 10). The owner state is the source of truth and is not written to the URL on the click itself.
detail: Never re-apply the owner's stale value on a timer: it undid ticks. Selection clears after a successful bulk action.

rule: Bulk bar appears only with a selection and only for users with edit permission. Each button is disabled with an explanatory tooltip when it would be a no-op or unsafe; every write shows a confirm dialog ('Confirm Pause 3 Campaigns' + consequence sentence); irreversible actions (Archive) say so; all buttons disable while a write is in flight.
detail: Partial results: toast with Successful / Failed counts and a detail/error file; rows withheld client-side (e.g. adjusted budget out of range) are listed with the reason and not sent.

rule: Treat HTTP 200 as untrusted for writes: zero successes or a non-empty errors array is a rejection and must be shown as an error; partial success is warnings, not a clean success.
detail: On failure inline cells keep the typed value and say 'Not saved'; optimistic switches revert.

rule: Where the backend replaces a whole record (campaign, ad group), every edit sends the full original record with only the changed fields overridden, and the local cache is patched with the saved record so the next edit starts from fresh data.
detail: Whole-set arrays such as per-placement bidding must be upserted into, never assigned, or untouched members go out as zero.

rule: Validate on blur/submit with messages under each field; reveal errors top-down (touching a section marks earlier visible sections touched); disable the main submit button with a tooltip of up to 6 blockers; block submit until marketplace limits (budget/bid min-max) have loaded; keep entered values after an API error.
detail: Schemas with conditional rules must be built once headlessly after editing (a malformed conditional silently crashed a whole page).

rule: Names may not contain ! # % < > ; campaign name <=117 (128 when it equals Amazon's name), ad group <=244 (255 when Amazon's), SB ad group/ad name <=117, ad title <=32; keyword <=80 chars, <=10 words (negative phrase <=4); lists: 150 keywords/targets, 200 negatives, SD 150 contextual / 20 audiences; placement % 0-900, audience % 1-900; SP budget >=1 and <=1,000,000 per marketplace constraints; min bid 0.02, max 10,000 (bid <= budget in create).
detail: These come from marketplace constraints fetched per profile; hard-coded numbers are only fallbacks. seller-hub must read limits from Amazon/marketplace data, not copy numbers.

rule: 'Today', calendar ceiling, default ranges and start-date minimum use the profile/marketplace time zone, not the browser's. Future days are greyed. Compare range: End autofills Start + length of main range, End >= Start, sent only when both set. 'Life time' = fixed earliest date to today. Dashboards drop presets that make no sense (Home: no Life time; Inventory: custom only).
detail: Running campaigns: start date read-only.

rule: Active profile resolves URL param > saved choice > first of list; it is mirrored into the URL (replace) and a cookie; switching profiles invalidates all cached data; an unknown profileId in the URL opens a chooser dialog; navbar actions disable during the switch.
detail: Every request carries the profile id as header.

rule: Hide write controls (bulk bar, create buttons) when the user lacks edit permission; show them disabled with a reason when the permission exists but the entity forbids it (archived, ended, other portfolio, read-only on Amazon). A missing per-entity edit flag means not editable. While roles load, every check is false and screens must wait before showing 'no access'.
detail: Hiding a menu item is not access control; each route gates itself.

rule: Failures render as an in-place error card with a message and Retry (one failing table must not break its neighbours); API errors in dialogs show status, message and a 'copy error content' action; session expiry redirects to sign-in with a return path and a guard against loops.
detail: Empty-state sentences are specific per screen ('Nothing has been changed in this period.').

rule: Two modes: small tables export the visible rows client-side to xlsx (selected rows, visible columns only); large ones start a background job that replays the query server-side. A job centre shows progress, auto-downloads once across tabs, supports cancel and restore (creates a new job), caps selected rows at 1000.
detail: Failure/timeout messages are explicit ('Export took too long... try a shorter date range').

rule: Shared visual behaviour is changed once in the design system, not per call site; copy (headers, tooltips, metric definitions, option labels, messages) lives in data modules so wording changes in one place.
detail: Implementation note for seller-hub packages/ui.

rule: Keep opened tabs mounted but inactive so returning is instant; table props must be referentially stable; read route params as raw strings and write via a singleton router so the whole table does not re-render on every URL change.
detail: Measured: tab switch used to block the main thread ~2 s.

rule: Amazon's own spec check is the source of truth for video creatives; never validate video in the browser. Poll the asset every 2 s up to 30 times after register; approved program wins; otherwise show only the first failing counted program; block submit when failed or still checking, not when unavailable.
detail: Counted programs: SB video + portrait; SD video + landscape. Measured limits: duration 6-45 s, video >=1000 kbps, audio >=96 kbps, 44.1 kHz; SB frame rates 23.976/23.98/24/25/29.97/29.98/30, codecs h264/h265/hevc, 16:9 or 9:16; SD landscape >=1920x1080. Each failing rule is one human line built from the failure reason or the spec id.

rule: Sidebar collapsed by default, closes on route change on narrow screens, flyout submenus on wide screens; breadcrumbs on every page; page title per route; routes tolerate old links via redirects.
detail: Shell variants (new app shell, legacy chrome) are a migration artefact, not a requirement.

rule: Tokens never reach the browser: sign-in via server redirect with PKCE and state, session id in an httpOnly cookie, server-side refresh shortly before expiry, one in-flight refresh per session, proxy that rejects unsafe path segments, internal-only return paths.
detail: Matches D-BFF; legacy kept the session in process memory (lost on restart) — seller-hub should persist sessions.
